Hi Anna — thanks for sending these over and for the spreadsheet. Quick read-through and a couple of clarification items so we can move the invoices out of hold: 

1) Legal name match: The state certificate lists "Greenleaf Foundation" but your Entity_Billing_List.xlsx shows three legal billing names with separate EINs. To accept exemption for each invoice we need either:
   - a separate state exemption certificate for each legal entity, or
   - a single blanket certificate that explicitly names all three legal entities and their EINs.

2) Seller name on certificate: Our tax team requires the certificate to reference the seller as "Redwood Inference, Inc." (our legal entity). If the attached CA certificate references a different seller name or a marketplace intermediary, we will need additional documentation tying that intermediary to Redwood.

3) W-9 / IRS link: Because you are a tax-exempt org, we still require a copy of the W-9 equivalent (EIN verification) or confirmation of tax-exempt status for each billing entity. A copy of your IRS determination letter helps (thanks for that).

Marcus in Finance — can you confirm the minimum acceptance checklist (invoice release SLA once docs validated)?

I can also share a short acceptance form (PDF) your team can sign to streamline future releases.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Irene / Anna — a few operational items from Finance: 

- Minimum acceptance for invoice release: (1) state certificate that names the purchasing legal entity or lists all entities claiming the exemption; (2) IRS determination letter OR other proof of 501(c)(3) status; (3) confirmation of billing address/EIN on each invoice to match the documentation.
- If the CA certificate does not explicitly name the seller "Redwood Inference, Inc.", we can accept a notarized statement from the buyer referencing the certificate and tying it to Redwood, but that adds processing time and is not preferred.
- Once we receive signed acceptance (or entity-specific certificates), Finance will clear the hold within 48 business hours and release payment to the normal payment run.

If Greenleaf can provide a single blanket exemption document that lists all three legal entities and their EINs and references Redwood Inference, that would be the fastest path.

Marcus

Anna — thanks for the clear options and the attachments. To move quickly and protect both parties, Redwood can accept option B with the following steps: 

1) Please complete and sign the attached Redwood exemption acceptance form (redwood-exemption-acceptance-form.pdf) listing the three legal entities and their EINs. The form contains a short affirmation that the CA certificate and IRS determination cover the entities listed for sales tax exemption purposes for purchases from Redwood Inference.
2) Return the signed PDF to procurement@redwoodinference.com. A scanned signature is acceptable; notarization is not required for this temporary acceptance.
3) Once returned, Finance (Marcus) will validate the attachments against the signed form and clear the hold within 48 business hours; we will notify you when the invoices are released.

If Greenleaf prefers the revised state certificate instead, we can keep the hold but will expedite processing on receipt.

I'll attach the PDF form to this thread and copy revops to keep a record.
